brief: US consumer confidence fell to 81.9 in September, the lowest since April 2014, which GREED & fear reads as a warning of a Republican rout in the midterms despite the usual post-midterm rally pattern. Equities have shrugged off rising yields this year because AI-capex-driven earnings growth is strong (S&P 3Q26 EPS seen up 30.2% YoY, IT up 65.1%), but 10-year and 30-year yields hit their highest since 2002, reconfirming GREED & fear's thesis since March 2020 that G7 bonds are in a structural bear market. That bond rout has pushed the MOVE index back near its post-Iran-strike level, widened high-yield spreads, and lifted mortgage rates to 7.3%, hurting mortgage applications and the incumbent's economic approval. Core PCE printed cooler than expected, cutting priced year-end hikes to 30bp from 52bp, though a faster Warsh-led Fed could still push the long end higher. GREED & fear names AI capex returns, the G7 bond bear market, and Iran-China geopolitics as the three dominant issues, while China's new first-time-buyer mortgage subsidy failed to move its property index much.
